title: 真假金丝雀的博弈第15章
content_zh:
第15章 方总的答复

    方总的邮件是周二上午十点发过来的。

    我正坐在顾西辞办公室的沙发上翻许向平那份黑色档案的复印件，手机震了一下。顾西辞坐在办公桌后面，盯着电脑屏幕，表情看不出喜怒。他看了大概半分钟，然后把显示器转过来给我看。

    邮件很短，只有三段。第一段感谢顾氏团队在并购案中的专业配合。第二段确认尽调流程已经完成，合规部门没有异议。第三段只有一句话——“我方决定于下周一派遣签约团队赴顾氏，完成正式协议签署。”

    签了。方总签了。

    我把手里的档案放在沙发上，站起来走到窗边。二十六楼往下看，街上的车流像一条缓慢的河。三个月前我从顾家宴会厅走出来的时候，坐在老陈的车里看着窗外，脑子里一片空白。那时候我不知道自己能撑多久，只知道第二天早上九点要去顾氏报到。现在方总的邮件躺在我面前，并购案正式落地。这个项目我跟了全程——从会议室里那句临场发挥的分析，到林曼如茶会上的试探，到许向平在万盛会议室里低头签字，再到上周发布会上那个问我凭什么站在台上的记者。

    “你不高兴？”顾西辞的声音从身后传来。

    “高兴。但没我想象的那么高兴。”

    “为什么？”

    “因为方总签的是顾氏的合同。我跟顾氏的合同还剩不到三年。”

    他靠在椅背上，手指在桌面敲了两下。

    “你怕三年到了没下文？”

    “不是怕。是在算。”

    “算什么？”

    “算我还需要多长时间才能攒够自己开公司的钱。按目前的月薪加绩效，大概还需要两年半。但如果有额外项目——”

    “你想要额外项目？”

    “我想要一个属于我自己的客户。”

    他挑了一下眉毛。

    方总对顾氏的并购案已经落地，但他手里还有别的项目。上次饭局上他提过一嘴，他们集团在沪市那边正在筹备一个新业务板块，需要专业的商业情报和舆情分析。当时我没接话，因为那时候并购案还没签，我不能分心。但现在合同稳了，我可以分心了。

    顾西辞沉默了大概五六秒，然后说：“可以。方总下周来签约，签约之后的庆功宴上你自己跟他谈。能谈下来是你的本事，我不拦。”

    “你不怕我翅膀硬了飞走？”

    “你的合同还有将近三年。飞也是三年以后的事。”

    “那三年之内我谈下来的所有外部客户，算不算违反竞业条款？”

    “不算。合同只约束你不能去竞争对手那边。方总不是顾氏的竞争对手，方总是顾氏的合作伙伴。”他端起咖啡喝了一口，语气平淡得像在念合同条款，“你帮合作伙伴做项目，我不但不拦，还可以给你提供办公位。”

Chapter 15 Mr. Fang’s reply

    Mr. Fang’s email was sent at ten o’clock on Tuesday morning.

    I was sitting on the sofa in Gu Xici's office, flipping through a copy of Xu Xiangping's black file, when my phone vibrated. Gu Xici sat behind his desk, staring at the computer screen, his expression showing no emotion or anger. He looked at it for about half a minute, then turned the monitor over to me.

    The email was short, only three paragraphs. The first paragraph is to thank the Gu team for their professional cooperation in the merger and acquisition case. The second paragraph confirms that the due diligence process has been completed and the compliance department has no objections. There is only one sentence in the third paragraph - "We have decided to send a signing team to Gu's next Monday to complete the formal agreement signing."

    Signed. Mr. Fang signed it.

    I put the file in my hand on the sofa, stood up and walked to the window. Looking down from the 26th floor, the traffic on the street is like a slow river. When I walked out of the Gu family banquet hall three months ago, I sat in Lao Chen's car and looked out the window, my mind going blank. At that time, I didn't know how long I could hold on. I only knew that I had to report to Gu's at nine o'clock the next morning. Now Mr. Fang’s email is lying in front of me, and the merger and acquisition case has officially been completed. I followed the entire process of this project - from the impromptu analysis in the conference room, to Lin Manru's test at the tea party, to Xu Xiangping bowing his head to sign in the Wansheng conference room, to the reporter at last week's press conference who asked me why I was standing on the stage.

    "Are you unhappy?" Gu Xici's voice came from behind.

    "Happy. But not as happy as I thought."

    "Why?"

    "Because Mr. Fang signed Gu's contract. My contract with Gu has less than three years left."

    He leaned back in his chair and tapped his fingers on the table twice.

    "Are you afraid that there will be no progress after three years?"

    "It's not fear. It's calculation."

    "What?"

    "Calculate how long it will take me to save enough money to start my own company. Based on the current monthly salary plus performance, it will take about two and a half years. But if there are additional projects-"

    "You want extra items?"

    "I wanted a client of my own."

    He raised an eyebrow.

    Mr. Fang's merger and acquisition of Gu's has been completed, but he has other projects in hand. He mentioned at the last dinner that their group was preparing a new business segment in the Shanghai Stock Exchange and needed professional business intelligence and public opinion analysis. I didn't answer the call at that time because the merger hadn't been signed yet and I couldn't be distracted. But now that the contract is secure, I can distract myself.

    Gu Xici was silent for about five or six seconds, and then said, "Okay. President Fang will come to sign the contract next week. You can talk to him yourself at the celebration banquet after the signing. It's your ability to negotiate, and I won't stop you."

    "Aren't you afraid that my wings will stiffen and I will fly away?"

    "You still have nearly three years on your contract. Flying will be three years from now."

    "Does all the external clients I negotiated with within the past three years be considered a violation of the non-competition clause?"

    "It doesn't count. The contract only restricts you from going to your competitors. Mr. Fang is not Gu's competitor. Mr. Fang is always Gu's partner." He took a sip of coffee and said in a calm tone, as if he was reading the terms of the contract, "If you help your partners with projects, I will not only not stop you, but I will also provide you with an office space."
title_en: The Game of True and False Canaries Chapter 15
